description: We are two students from Casablanca, Morocco. We chose this challenge because of where we live: in 2011 a piece of Mars fell out of the sky near Tissint, and we grew up a few hours from one of the most Mars-like deserts on Earth. So we spent the hackathon teaching a machine to scan our own country with NASA's data — and it surprised us: its top discovery was a place neither of us had ever heard of. RED ATLAS is our answer. Open source, bilingual, and built so that any country can rerun it and find its own analogs.
summary: We are two students from Casablanca. We kept reading that space agencies fly teams 10,000+ km to Chile or Iceland to rehearse for the Moon and Mars — while we live three hours from one of the most Mars-like deserts on Earth. So we asked a simple question: if you scan all of Morocco with NASA's own climate data, which places truly behave like the Moon and Mars? Instead of hand-picking sites, we wrote an engine that sampled 159 points across the country through the NASA POWER API and scored each one on the four things mission planners actually care about: day-night temperature swings (against Curiosity's ~60 °C at Gale Crater), aridity, wind and solar radiation. Then we let k-means clustering rank them — and our favourite moment came when the machine's number-one spot, the Guelmim-Assa steppe, turned out to be on nobody's list. It also re-found Tafilalet, where analog crews already train, all by itself. In the app, anyone can click any point on Earth and get its analog fingerprint. Erg Chebbi's 31.0 °C swing matches the Atacama (31.1 °C); M'hamid is hotter than Death Valley. Don't take our word for it: engine/verify.py checks every number live against NASA's API.
details: WHY WE CHOSE THIS CHALLENGE — In 2011, a piece of Mars fell out of the sky near Tissint, Morocco — one of the few Martian meteorites ever witnessed. Austrian analog crews trained here for MARS2013, and the Ibn Battuta Centre has tested ExoMars instruments for years. Yet Africa still has no permanent analog research station, and agencies keep flying 10,000+ km to Chile, Canada or Iceland. We wanted to know: does the data agree that Morocco belongs on that list? WHAT WE BUILT — RED ATLAS is a live web app plus an open analysis engine. (1) The Analog Engine sampled 159 points across Morocco on a 0.5 degree grid through the NASA POWER API, then scored each point with a Mars Likeness Index — an equal-weight mean of four scores: thermal cycling vs Gale Crater's ~60 °C swing, aridity, aeolian wind, and solar load. The formula is published and the code is open. (2) We deliberately let k-means clustering (k=3) find the zones instead of picking them ourselves. Its top discovery, the Guelmim-Assa steppe (MLI 79.9), was on none of our lists — and it independently re-found the field-proven Tafilalet. (3) Analyze Anywhere: click any point on Earth for live NASA POWER climatology, MLI/TSI scores, and an AI-agent verdict that always ends with one honest limitation. (4) Zone Analysis: draw a rectangle, get a full report from a 5-point sample, cross-checked against the engine's grid. THE SCIENCE, HONESTLY — Our Thermal Stress Index compares each site's day-night swing to Gale Crater. Erg Chebbi (31.0 °C) equals the Atacama (31.1 °C). M'hamid's July maximum (46.9 °C) beats Death Valley (46.2 °C). The Moon comparison uses LRO Diviner swings (poles ~60 °C vs equator ~260 °C). And we say clearly, in numbers, what Morocco cannot replicate: gravity, atmosphere, radiation, polar cold. Every headline number is checked by engine/verify.py — 9/9 live checks against NASA's API, rerun it yourself. DATA AND TOOLS — NASA POWER API (all Earth climate data, pre-computed and live), NASA Worldview (MODIS imagery), MSL Curiosity/REMS (Mars reference), LRO Diviner (lunar reference), NASA SRTM (elevations), Earthdata and PDS for discovery. Partners: ESA Copernicus (Sentinel-2 per site), CSA RADARSAT and Esri World Imagery for terrain context. Built with vanilla JS, Leaflet, Chart.js, a Python engine (stdlib + numpy), Vercel serverless functions for the AI agent, PWA offline, bilingual EN/FR. WHAT IT COULD BECOME — The engine's siting algorithm picked the Anti-Atlas corridor (29.3°N, 8.5°W) as the optimal location for an Atlas Analog Station. Phase 0 needs 90 days and under $500: three thermal loggers at Erg Chebbi, Agoudal and the Guelmim-Assa discovery, ground truth vs NASA POWER, publish the delta — exactly how analog sites get scientifically validated. OPEN SOURCE — MIT license: https://github.com/sara-zeroual/red-atlas — Live app: https://red-atlas-pi.vercel.app/ — The engine is not Morocco-specific: any country can rerun it to find its own analogs.
